newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM IN TALKS TO BUY U.S. DAUBERT UNITS.
newsitem.headline: UPM IN TALKS TO BUY U.S. DAUBERT UNITS.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said in a statement on Tuesday it was in talks about buying U.S. siliconised paper producer Daubert Coated Products Inc's release paper and consumer products units.
"The turnover of the business to be purchased is about $70 million," UPM-Kymmene said.
"The purchase will strengthen the global position of Lohjan Paperi as one of the world's leading siliconised paper producers," UPM-Kymmene said. Lohjan Paperi is a fully-owned subsidiary.
Lohjan Paperi managing director Jussi Virkkunen told Reuters by telephone that the deal was "very likely" to be concluded by the autumn and that the operation was profitable.
Virkkunen said he expected the price to be "below net sales" and that the investment would meet UPM's required return on investment of between 15 and 20 percent.

"What we really wanted here was the release paper unit, the consumer products (which makes adhesive tapes) is coming more or less on the side," he said, adding that the tape operation was also profitable.
The unit would also help Lohja sell its own siliconised products in the U.S., Virkkunen said.
"It will make it possible for us to expand on the U.S. market, also with Lohja's own products," he said.
"This will make us number two globally on the siliconised paper market," he said, adding Rexham was the biggest.
Virkkunen said Daubert would maintain operations with net sales of about $30 million.
